How do I get the scan working again?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "18e20851-9949-4218-841e-f07511863776", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Windows Server EC2 patch scan hanging recovery"}]}

{"id": "c61f0135-560b-4d7a-bca4-c54589e49c2e", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is a classic Windows Update Agent (WUA) corruption scenario on Server 2016 — the symptoms you're describing (stuck `wuauserv` in "Stopping", `TiWorker.exe`/`svchost.exe` pegged near 100% CPU for an extended period, and a bloated `DataStore.edb` over 1GB) point to a corrupted or oversized WUA datastore that's causing the service to churn through scan/compaction logic without finishing. Here's how to recover it, in order of least to most invasive:

## 1. Confirm it's actually stuck (not just slow)
Before killing anything, check:
- `Get-Service wuauserv` — note the status
- Task Manager / `Get-Process TiWorker, svchost | Select Id, CPU` — confirm sustained near-100% CPU for over an hour (not a brief spike)
- Check `%windir%\WindowsUpdate.log` or `Get-WindowsUpdateLog` output for the last logged activity timestamp — if it's frozen with no new entries, the scan is genuinely hung, not just slow on a huge datastore.

## 2. Stop the stuck services (force if needed)
```powershell
Stop-Service wuauserv -Force
Stop-Service bits -Force
Stop-Service cryptsvc -Force
```
If `wuauserv` won't leave "Stopping" state, kill the underlying process:
```powershell
Get-Process TiWorker,svchost | Where-Object {$_.Modules.ModuleName -contains "wuaueng.dll"}
# then as last resort:
taskkill /PID <wuauserv_svchost_pid> /F
```
A reboot is often faster and safer than fighting a wedged service — if you can tolerate downtime, reboot the instance first and see if services come up clean.

## 3. Rename/reset the SoftwareDistribution folder (this is almost certainly your fix)
A 1GB+ `DataStore.edb` is well beyond healthy (normal is tens to a few hundred MB). It's a strong sign the WUA datastore is corrupted or needs an offline defrag that's never completing online.

```powershell
Stop-Service wuauserv -Force
Stop-Service bits -Force
Stop-Service cryptsvc -Force

Rename-Item "$env:windir\SoftwareDistribution" "SoftwareDistribution.old"

Start-Service cryptsvc
Start-Service bits
Start-Service wuauserv
```
This forces WUA to rebuild a fresh `DataStore.edb` on next scan. You lose update history/cache (re-downloads needed) but it resolves corruption-driven hangs reliably.

## 4. If renaming doesn't fix it, try ESENT repair/defrag directly
Since the datastore is edb-based (ESE/Jet), you can attempt an offline repair instead of nuking it (useful if you want to preserve history):
```cmd
esentutl /p "%windir%\SoftwareDistribution\DataStore.edb"
esentutl /d "%windir%\SoftwareDistribution\DataStore.edb"
```
Run with `wuauserv` stopped. In practice, most people skip this and just rename the folder — it's faster and the datastore self-rebuilds.

## 5. Re-register WUA components (if scans still won't start after the reset)
```cmd
net stop wuauserv
net stop cryptsvc
regsvr32 /s wuaueng.dll
regsvr32 /s wuapi.dll
regsvr32 /s wucltui.dll
net start cryptsvc
net start wuauserv
```

## 6. Check for the known root causes on Server 2016 specifically
- **Missing SHA-2 code signing update** (KB4474419) — pre-2019 Server 2016 images without this will hang/fail WUA scans indefinitely against modern update servers. This is a very common cause of exactly this symptom set.
- **SSU (Servicing Stack Update) out of date** — install the latest SSU before retrying the scan.
- If this is WSUS-managed, check client-side targeting and WSUS server health too — a WSUS-side issue can also manifest as endless client-side scanning.

## A note on next steps
Given this is a live hung instance, I can pull CloudWatch/SSM data on it if you want — e.g. recent CPU/memory metrics, or check SSM command history for prior patch attempts — to help confirm root cause before you intervene.
